Visit note | 2025-05-21 03:00 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Sanjida Howlader, 46, female. Mrs. Howlader visits because she feels her hands shaking, has been losing weight despite eating well, and feels very uncomfortable in hot weather. She works as a ride-share driver and first noticed these troubles during a hot summer in Khulna. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She reports no chest pain or vision changes. On examination: pulse 116 bpm, BP 133/77 mmHg, weight 46 kg. Her thyroid gland is slightly enlarged and smooth without nodules. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee and to rest when her heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-05-21 03:00 PM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Wasim Howlader, 27, male. Mr. Howlader attends complaining of frequent sneezing fits and nasal symptoms that become much worse around dust. He works as a ride-share driver and explains that these flare-ups occur each spring in Badda. He has no known chronic illnesses and denies fever or facial pain. On examination: about 9 sneezing fits a day, BP 136/83 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 88 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy with clear secretions. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash his bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-05-21 04:00 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Sabina Akand, 78, female. Mrs. Akand presents with a long history of smoking, producing more sputum than usual, and breathlessness that has been worsening for several days. She is a retired civil servant and states her breathing trouble worsened during the dusty dry season in Gazipur. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies chest pain or leg swelling. On examination: SpO2 90%, BP 120/75 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 86 kg. Chest auscultation reveals diffuse wheezing and prolonged expiration. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

He was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

She works as a farmer and notes these troubles started after a week of stagnant rainwater around her house in Chattogram. She has no chronic illnesses and denies cough or diarrhea. On examination: temperature 102.7°F, platelet count 131000 per microlitre, BP 133/79 mmHg, pulse 94 bpm, weight 50 kg. Skin shows a mild blanching rash over the forelimbs. Assessment: Dengue fever. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.
